Done. Created [ttl_cache.py](ttl_cache.py) and [test_ttl_cache.py](test_ttl_cache.py) — all 16 tests pass.

Implementation notes:
- Backed by an `OrderedDict` mapping key → (value, put_time); LRU order is maintained via `move_to_end` on `get` and re-insert on `put`.
- Expiry uses `now - put_time >= ttl` (boundary is exclusive of the live item), checked in `get`, `put` and `len`; expired entries are purged before eviction so they never push out live items.
- `capacity 0` short-circuits `put` (stores nothing); `ValueError` for `capacity < 0` or `ttl <= 0`.
- Tests use a fake clock to cover the exact expiry boundary, TTL refresh on re-put, LRU eviction (both `get` and `put` counting as use), and zero-capacity behavior.

Fixed — all 10 tests pass. Rewrote [confparse.py](confparse.py) and added [test_confparse.py](test_confparse.py).

Changes:
- **`;` comments** ignored alongside `#`.
- **Values with `=`** use `partition("=")` instead of `split("=")`, so `a=b=c` → `a = "b=c"`.
- **Quotes** (`"..."` / `'...'`) stripped only when they wrap the whole value — inner spaces preserved (`"hello  world"` keeps double spaces).
- **Sections** lowercased and merged (`[Main]`/`[main]` → `main`); re-opening an existing section appends to it.
- **Repeated keys**: last value wins (plain dict assignment).
- **Keys before any section** go into a `default` section (created up front).
- **Indented continuation lines** append to the last key's value, joined with single spaces (works after quoted values too).
- **Line without `=`** raises `ValueError("line 3: missing '='")` with the 1-based line number; a continuation line with no preceding key also raises with its line number.

Done — all 51 tests pass.

- [tokcount.py](tokcount.py) — `parse_count(text) -> int`. A single regex captures the number and optional suffix; then:
  - **No suffix**: only `\d+` with space/comma thousands groups (`1 000 000`, `1,000,000`) accepted; anything with a stray dot/comma (`1,00`, `1.5`, `1.2.3`) raises `ValueError`.
  - **With suffix** (`k/K`, `m/M`, `b/B`, Russian `к`, `тыс`, `м`, `млн`, case-insensitive, spaces allowed around): exactly one decimal point or decimal comma is allowed before the suffix (`1.5M`, `1,5M`, `1,25 тыс`). Fractional results that aren't whole (`1,0001k` → 1000.1) raise `ValueError`; arithmetic uses `Decimal` so there are no float rounding surprises.
  - Negatives, unknown suffixes, empty/garbage input, and non-strings all raise `ValueError`.
- [test_tokcount.py](test_tokcount.py) — 51 parametrized tests: 23 valid cases, 26 invalid cases, plus non-string input and fractional-result checks.

One fix along the way: my first regex didn't allow grouped separators inside the number (`1 000 000` failed); the final pattern `\d+(?:[ ,]\d{3})*(?:[.,]\d+)?` handles both separators and the decimal part, with a stricter fullmatch check per branch.

Fixed and all 8 tests pass.

**[bizdays.py](file:bizdays.py)** — rewritten:
- Counts Mon–Fri days over the inclusive range `[start, end]` in O(1): `full_weeks * 5` plus a remainder of at most 6 days checked individually — no day-by-day loop, so a 100-year range is instant.
- Holidays: deduplicated via a set, only subtracted if they fall inside the range on a weekday (weekend holidays change nothing).
- Reversed order: swaps the endpoints and returns the negated count.
- Datetimes: reduced to `.date()` for start/end and holidays, so only the date part matters.

**[test_bizdays.py](file:test_bizdays.py)** — 8 tests: full week, single weekday/weekend day, both-ends-included, negative on reversal, holiday edge cases (weekend holiday, duplicates, out-of-range), mixed date/datetime inputs, the 100-year range, and 300 randomized cases cross-checked against a naive day-by-day reference implementation.

One note: my first version of the 100-year test used a hand-computed constant that was wrong (the function was right); the test now verifies against the naive reference instead.

Done — 98 tests pass.

- [tokcount.py](tokcount.py) — `parse_count(text) -> int`. Handles space/comma thousands grouping, decimal dot/comma before a suffix, suffixes `k/m/b` and Russian `к/тыс/м/млн` (case-insensitive, spaces allowed), strips surrounding spaces. Raises `ValueError` for empty input, signs/negatives, unknown suffixes, several dots, decimals without a suffix, and bad comma usage like `1,00` (no suffix) or `1,0000`.
- [test_tokcount.py](test_tokcount.py) — parametrized valid/invalid cases for plain numbers, suffixes, and non-string inputs.

Two notes on judgment calls I made (both covered by tests): `1,00k` / `1.0k` are accepted, since a single dot/comma directly before a suffix is a decimal separator per the spec — only bare `1,00` is rejected; and very large space-grouped numbers like `1 000 000 000` are accepted as long as every group after the first has exactly 3 digits.

Fixed. [bizdays.py](file:bizdays.py) now counts Mon–Fri days with both ends included, in O(1) arithmetic (full weeks × 5 plus a check of at most 6 leftover days) — no day-by-day loop, so a 100-year range is instant. Holidays are deduplicated via a set, weekend holidays are skipped, holidays outside the range are ignored, datetimes are accepted (date part only), and a reversed range returns the negated count.

Tests in [test_bizdays.py](file:test_bizdays.py): 15 passing, including edge cases (single day, full weeks, weekend holiday, duplicate holidays, negative direction, datetimes) and a 300-case randomized comparison against a naive day-by-day reference implementation. One note: my initial hardcoded constant for the 100-year test was wrong (26088 vs the true 26090) — I recomputed it with the naive reference and fixed the test, not the implementation.

Done — all 11 tests pass.

- [ttl_cache.py](file:ttl_cache.py) — `TTLCache` built on an `OrderedDict` mapping key → (value, put_time). Expired items are purged lazily on every operation (from the front, oldest put first, stopping at the first live item), so they're never returned, don't count in `len()`, and never occupy capacity. LRU order is maintained by `move_to_end` on `get` and delete-and-reinsert on `put`; `capacity 0` stores nothing; `ValueError` for `capacity < 0` or `ttl <= 0`.
- [test_ttl_cache.py](file:test_ttl_cache.py) — covers validation, capacity 0, LRU eviction (get and re-put both count as use), exact expiry boundary (`now - put_time >= ttl`), expired items not counted or evicting live ones, TTL reset on re-put, and delete of missing keys — using an injectable fake clock.

All 9 tests pass. [confparse.py](confparse.py) is fixed for every reported bug:

- **`;` comments** are skipped (along with `#` and blanks).
- **`=` in values** — splits only on the first `=` (`split("=", 1)`), so `url = http://x/?a=1&b=2` works.
- **Quoted values** — matching `"` or `'` pairs are stripped, inner spaces preserved (`"hello  world"` → `hello  world`).
- **Case-insensitive sections** — `[Main]` and `[main]` merge into one lowercase `main` section.
- **Duplicate keys** — last value wins (plain dict assignment).
- **Keys before any section** go into a `default` section, created lazily so it doesn't pollute output when unused (the original `test_simple` still passes).
- **Indented continuation lines** append to the previous key's value, joined with single spaces (`one\n    two\n    three` → `one two three`).
- **Lines without `=`** raise `ValueError: line 3: expected 'key = value'` with the 1-based line number.

[test_confparse.py](test_confparse.py) now has one test per case (9 total), all green.

Fixed — all 31 tests pass.

**What was wrong:** the old loop used `while d < end` (end excluded) and was O(days).

**New [bizdays.py](file:bizdays.py):**
- Closed-form weekday count: full weeks × 5 plus a remainder check over ≤6 days — O(1) in range length, so a 100-year span is instant (verified: 1924→2024 gives 26090, matching a day-by-day reference).
- Both ends included; reversed range returns the negated count.
- Holidays: deduplicated via `set`, only subtracted when they fall inside the range on a weekday — weekend holidays and duplicates change nothing.
- Datetimes accepted for `start`, `end` and holidays (`.date()` extracted); dates and datetimes can be mixed.

**Tests** in [test_bizdays.py](file:test_bizdays.py): edge cases (single day, weekend-only span, both-ends inclusion, negation, weekend/duplicate/out-of-range holidays, datetime inputs), the 100-year case, and 20 randomized ranges cross-checked against a naive day-by-day reference implementation in both directions.

One note: my first hardcoded 100-year expectation (52171) was wrong — I verified the correct value (26090) against the naive reference before fixing the test.
